# Rex plans

A Rex plan is one unit of work (a feature, a fix, a migration) saved as JSON at `rex/plans/<name>.rex.json` in the repo, committed with the code. Rex shows it as an outline next to the agent tape, pins one task at a time, and turns it into a send-off brief for the next chat. You write the plan as an ordinary file. Rex never sends you anything; a person copies briefs into chat.

The format is frozen at `"version": 1`; the full contract is `docs/plan-format.md` in the Rex repo.

## When to plan

- You are asked to plan, to break work down, or to fill or refine a `.rex.json`.
- The work is bigger than one PR. One plan per unit of work; a second feature gets its own file.
- Do not create a plan for a one-line fix, and do not add tasks for work nobody asked for.

## The shape

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "id": "card-highlight",
  "title": "Selected plan card is one block",
  "goal": "One paragraph: what this work is for and what will be true when it is done.",
  "status": "pending",
  "base": "main",
  "scope": {
    "in": ["the hard edges of the job"],
    "out": ["what this work must not touch"]
  },
  "tasks": [
    {
      "id": "card-bar",
      "title": "Bar spans the whole card",
      "parent": "",
      "status": "pending",
      "needs": ["what must already be true before starting"],
      "does": ["what will be true when this task is done"],
      "description": "longer intent, only if title and does are not enough",
      "depends_on": [],
      "verify": ["go test ./internal/tui -run PlanCard", "Open latest: ▌ on all three card rows"],
      "files": ["internal/tui/plans.go"],
      "branch": "feature/card_bar",
      "scope": {"in": [], "out": []},
      "accomplished": [],
      "modified": [],
      "verified_how": [],
      "completed_notes": ""
    }
  ]
}
```

Plan fields: `version`, `id`, `title`, `goal`, `status`, `base`, `scope` (`in`, `out`), `tasks`.
Task fields: `id`, `title`, `parent`, `status`, `scope`, `needs`, `does`, `description`, `depends_on`, `verify`, `files`, `branch`, and the completion fields `accomplished`, `modified`, `verified_how`, `completed_notes`.

## Rules

- **ids** are short, stable slugs (`card-bar`). Never renumber or reuse them; other tasks and send-offs refer to them.
- **The tasks array is flat**, in the order the work should be done, which is also the order its PRs stack. Do not nest `children`.
- **`parent`** is outline: the task sits under that heading. **`depends_on`** is order: hard prerequisites only, the tasks that must be `done` (or `skipped`) first, always earlier in the file. They are independent; a task can sit under "UI" and depend on a task under "storage".
- Only leaf tasks (nobody's parent) get pinned. Keep the outline two or three levels deep; deeper means a second plan.
- **One task, one PR** a human can review in one sitting. If it is bigger, split it.
- **`needs` vs `does`.** `needs` is what must already be true ("the pick colors exist"); `does` is what will be true when the task is done ("the bar spans all three rows"). Keep them apart; merged, nobody can tell "we still lack X" from "we will ship X".
- **`verify`** is how a stranger would check it: commands or observations. **`files`** are the paths or globs the task will edit. They are not a lock, but Rex reads them: an edit outside every folder the pinned task lists shows as drift, so list each folder the task really touches.
- **`scope.out`** is the hard edge: what this work must not touch. Rex matches its entries against prompts and edited paths, so write short nouns or path words ("extra palettes", "web UI", "internal/jsonedit/**"), not sentences ("do not change the public API of …").
- **`status`** is one of `pending`, `active`, `done`, `blocked`, `skipped`. At most one leaf task (one that is nobody's `parent`) is `active`: that is the pin. A parent marked `active` is only a label. Write status down; do not leave it to be inferred.

## Stacked PRs

Rex never runs git or opens a PR. A plan can still be shaped so each task lands as one PR in a stack, and the send-off then tells whoever works the pinned task where its PR goes.

- **Opt in with `base`**: the branch the stack lands on, the trunk this repo starts work from (its agents.md or CONTRIBUTING says; else `git symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` minus `origin/`). A plan that builds on another unmerged stack names that stack's top branch.
- **One leaf task, one PR.** Parents are headings, never PRs, and get no `branch`. `skipped` tasks have no PR.
- **The stack is file order.** The first leaf's PR targets `base`; each next leaf's targets the branch of the leaf before it. Each task builds and passes its tests on the tasks before it alone, and `depends_on` names only earlier tasks; Rex reports one that points later.
- **One plan, one stack.** Tasks that need none of each other's code still stack, in the order they should land. Work that must merge on its own goes in its own plan.
- **`branch`**: name every leaf's branch up front, the way this repo names branches (`feature/card_bar` here). Plain names only: letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`, `/`, at most 80 bytes; Rex leaves any other name out of the commands it writes. One per task, never the same as `base`.
- **Changing a stack.** Reorder freely before work starts. Once branches exist, add new work as a new task at the end rather than moving one, and fix a lower PR with a commit on its branch.

## Never in a plan

- prompts, system prompts or nudges for an agent;
- auto-approve lists or tool permissions;
- diffs or file bodies;
- secrets;
- timestamps that change on every save.

## Working a task from a send-off

A send-off brief names the plan file and the pinned task, and ends with a `rex-sendoff:` line naming the plan and the task. Work only on that task, stay inside its scope and out of the plan's `scope.out`, and if the plan is wrong, edit the JSON rather than working around it.

**Always end your final reply with these lines**, so Rex can prefill the completion and knows which task the reply is about:

```
accomplished: <what you actually did, one line>
verified: <how you checked it, one line>
rex-sendoff: <the same line as at the end of the brief>
```

### Its PR, when the send-off has a Stack part

Do these steps when the repo's own rules for a PR are met (its checks, review and PR body):

1. **Cut.** Create the `Branch:` from the `Base:` branch (`git switch -c <branch> <base>`). If it already exists (an earlier chat started it, or the task was reopened), switch to it and add commits rather than amending them. If it isn't on the base yet (the base moved, or a lower task finished since), rebase it onto the base and retarget its PR. If the PR below has merged, cut from the plan's `base`; after a squash merge, move an existing branch with `git rebase --onto <plan base> <old base> <branch>`. If the PR below was closed without merging, stop and ask.
2. **Record.** If the plan has no branch for this task, or you used another name, write it as this task's `"branch"`, touching nothing else.
3. **Keep one plan.** Rex reads the plan file from the working tree, so it must not change when you switch branches. It is the stack's, not one PR's: commit its changes (your `branch`, Rex's status writes, a retrospective) only on the top branch of the stack, never on a lower one. Keep it as it is across every branch switch: copy it out of the repo, `git checkout -- <plan>`, switch, and copy it back.
4. **Open.** Push and open the PR against the base, not the trunk. In the body, put the `rex-sendoff:` line, the PR it sits on, and that the stack merges bottom-up. On GitHub: `gh pr create --base <base> --head <branch>`.
5. **Link.** On GitHub with the `github/gh-stack` extension: `gh stack link --base <plan base> <every branch of the stack from the bottom> <branch>`, as the send-off spells it. `--base` is the base of the first branch listed, and link corrects the PR bases it is given, so never start the list in the middle. Leave out branches whose PR merged. Without the extension, or on GitLab, Gitea or Bitbucket, the chain of base branches is the stack: open each PR or MR against the one below, and merge bottom-up. Don't install extensions unless asked.
6. **Restack.** If the send-off lists `PRs above it`, your commits moved what they sit on. After pushing, check out the top branch and run `git rebase --autostash --update-refs <your branch>` (Git 2.38+; it moves every branch in between, and `--autostash` keeps the plan file's changes), then `git push --force-with-lease` each moved branch, and check that the PR just above targets your branch. Leave out any whose PR merged.

## Marking a task done

Usually the person marks the task done in Rex (`d⏎`), which writes `"status": "done"` plus `accomplished`, `modified` and `verified_how` from your trailer and what Rex saw. Only when you are asked to complete it yourself, set that task's `status` to `done` and fill:

- `accomplished`: what actually happened (a retrospective, not a copy of `does`);
- `modified`: the paths you actually changed;
- `verified_how`: how you actually checked it;
- `completed_notes`: anything the next send-off should know.

Leave `branch` as it is: the next send-off finds the PR below by it. Edit only that task's object, keep every other byte of the file as it is, and never mark a task done that you did not finish. If every leaf task is now `done` or `skipped`, also set the plan's own top-level `status` to `done`; parent tasks don't need a status of their own.
